This small piece of land, only about a quarter of a timad, carries my enset and a few coffee trees my father planted. I do not buy fertilizer from the cooperative for this plot — the bag is too big for such a small patch, and I would rather use it on my maize if I had cash. What I do is carry the cattle manure and kitchen ash to the enset holes, the way everyone in my village does, because enset grows well with manure and needs little else. I weed it myself with my wife when we have time, and I do not need to hire anyone for such a small plot.
